content.user_title: Export Java Telemetry to Azure Monitor
content.value_statement: Java teams need clear guidance for sending OpenTelemetry data to Azure Monitor. This skill explains exporter setup, recommended migration, spans, metrics, and safe configuration choices.
actual_capabilities: Explains Maven dependencies for the deprecated exporter and the recommended autoconfigure package.
Shows how to configure Azure Monitor through an environment variable or explicit connection string.
Demonstrates spans, attributes, nested spans, exception recording, counters, and histograms.
Covers custom SpanProcessor registration with the OpenTelemetry SDK builder.
Links to migration, Maven, OpenTelemetry Java, and Application Insights references.
limitations: The documented exporter is deprecated, so new projects should prefer autoconfigure.
It does not install packages, run builds, or validate Azure resources.
Example connection strings use placeholders; users must provide secure real values.
The guidance focuses on Java and does not cover other OpenTelemetry languages.

use_cases.title: Migrate Telemetry Setup
use_cases.description: Plan a move from the deprecated exporter to Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry autoconfigure.

use_cases.title: Standardize Observability Guidance
use_cases.description: Create consistent instructions for tracing, metrics, and exception recording in Java services.

use_cases.title: Review Instrumentation Design
use_cases.description: Check whether spans, attributes, counters, and histograms match Azure Monitor reporting needs.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Migration Path
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner user learning why the package changed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Exporter Java skill. Explain why this exporter is deprecated and summarize the recommended autoconfigure migration for my Java service.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Tracing
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer adding spans to a Java workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline basic Azure Monitor tracing for a Java operation. Include span naming, attributes, exception recording, and when to end spans.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Metrics Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Team defining counters and latency measurements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design Java OpenTelemetry metrics for request counts and latency. Explain useful metric names, units, and attributes for Azure Monitor.

prompt_templates.title: Review Advanced Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Java OpenTelemetry setup for Azure Monitor. Check custom SpanProcessor use, nested spans, exception handling, metrics, and migration risks.

output_examples.input: I need to migrate a Java service from the deprecated exporter.
output_examples.output: The response explains the deprecation, recommends the autoconfigure package, lists dependency changes, and highlights configuration updates to review.

output_examples.input: I want to add tracing to order processing.
output_examples.output: The response proposes span names, useful order attributes, exception recording behavior, and scope handling guidance.

output_examples.input: I need metrics for HTTP requests and latency.
output_examples.output: The response suggests a request counter, a latency histogram, units, and attributes that support Azure Monitor analysis.

best_practices: Prefer Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry autoconfigure for new Java work and migrations.
Store real connection strings in secure configuration, not source files or prompts.
Use meaningful span names, semantic attributes, exception recording, and reliable span endings.
anti_patterns: Starting new production work on the deprecated exporter without a migration plan.
Hardcoding real instrumentation keys or connection strings in application code.
Creating spans without ending them or recording failures when exceptions occur.

faq.question: Is this skill for the current Azure Monitor Java package?
faq.answer: It documents the deprecated exporter and recommends migration to Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry autoconfigure.

faq.question: Can it configure my Azure resource automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but it does not create or modify Azure resources.

faq.question: Does it include tracing examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers spans, attributes, nested spans, scope handling, and exception recording.

faq.question: Does it include metrics examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes counters and histograms for request counts and latency measurement.

faq.question: Should I paste real connection strings into prompts?
faq.answer: No. Use placeholders in prompts and store real values in secure environment configuration.
